title: Bangsaen42 Chonburi Marathon 2026 Review: What the Race Is Like
meta_description: Bangsaen42 review: a marathon-only, World Athletics Elite Label race on a flat coastal course at Bang Saen, grown from 6,000 to 12,500+ runners since 2017.
dek: Bangsaen42 is a marathon-only race on the Gulf of Thailand coast in Chonburi. Here is what the race is like, from its recent editions, ahead of the 2026 edition.
verdict: Unlike many big races, Bangsaen42 offers only the full marathon, and it is built for running well. It carries a World Athletics Elite Label, and its course follows the coastal roads of Bang Saen on a largely flat profile, with a bridge section the only real rise [1]. It was first run in 2017 with about 6,000 runners and has grown to more than 12,500 in recent editions, with a seven-hour cut-off [1]. The 2025 race was run on 9 November. If you want a certified, flat marathon by the sea in Thailand, it is a strong choice. The account here is a general race profile, not a report on a single edition.

sections.heading: What the Race Is Like
paragraphs: The race starts near the Bangsaen Heritage Hotel at dawn, with the Gulf of Thailand alongside [1]. The early kilometres follow Bangsaen Beach, and the route continues on coastal roads past local landmarks including Ang Sila Market and the Nezha shrine at Naklua [1].
A bridge section gives views over the sea without much climbing, and the rest of the course is largely flat, which suits even pacing [1]. The cut-off is seven hours [1].

sections.heading: Growth and Recognition
paragraphs: Bangsaen42 was first held in 2017 as a standalone marathon, with about 6,000 runners [1]. It has since grown to more than 12,500 participants [1]. It holds the World Athletics Elite Label, and is organised by MICE & Communication, which also runs the Bangsaen21 Half Marathon [1].
The race profile credits it with extensive hydration and medical support, live runner tracking and a large volunteer network along the course [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a flat, certified marathon in Thailand with a real field. The marathon-only format means everyone on the road is running the full distance.
Pace for the climate. Even on a coastal course in November, Chonburi can be warm and humid, so use the sea breeze but do not count on it.
This review is compiled from a race profile describing recent editions. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: What distances does Bangsaen42 offer?
faqs.answer: Only the full marathon, 42.195 km. Unlike many big races, it has no shorter distances on the day. The half marathon is a separate event, Bangsaen21, run by the same organiser.

faqs.question: Is the Bangsaen42 course flat?
faqs.answer: Largely. It follows the coastal roads of Bang Saen in Chonburi, starting near the Bangsaen Heritage Hotel, with a bridge section the only notable rise. The cut-off is seven hours.

faqs.question: How big is Bangsaen42?
faqs.answer: More than 12,500 participants in recent editions, up from about 6,000 at the first race in 2017. It carries a World Athletics Elite Label.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28. Replaces a pre-race preview. No detailed report on the 9 November 2025 race could be read, so this is written from a race profile describing recent editions, and says so. No rating.
